messages.content:
## Schema and Missing Values Summary

### students.csv (18 rows × 6 columns)
| Column | Dtype | Description |
|---|---|---|
| student_id | int64 | Numeric student identifier (range 101–106) |
| name | object | Student name (6 unique, e.g., Alice) |
| subject | object | Subject (3 unique, e.g., Math) |
| score | int64 | Test score (range 55–95, mean 78.5) |
| grade_level | int64 | Grade level (range 10–12, mean ~10.67) |
| attendance_pct | int64 | Attendance percentage (range 75–99, mean 89.5) |

**Missing values:** None. All 6 columns have a non-null count of 18, matching the total row count.

### sales.csv (15 rows × 5 columns)
| Column | Dtype | Description |
|---|---|---|
| region | object | Sales region (3 unique, e.g., EU) |
| product | object | Product name (2 unique, e.g., Widget) |
| quarter | object | Quarter (3 unique, e.g., Q1) |
| units | int64 | Units sold (range 30–200, mean ~101.67) |
| revenue | float64 | Revenue (range 570.0–3000.0, mean ~1456.67) |

**Missing values:** None. All 5 columns have a non-null count of 15, matching the total row count.

### Interpretation
Both datasets are clean and complete with no missing values. students.csv is a small relational-style table keyed by student_id with categorical fields (name, subject) and numeric metrics (score, grade_level, attendance_pct). sales.csv is a transactional-style table with categorical dimensions (region, product, quarter) and two numeric measures (units, revenue).
